A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAST research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original refusal-rate experiments across multiple language models, condition-composition experiments, and analyses of sample size, runtime, and unseen prompt categories.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the refusal rates in Tables 2–3 and experiments in Figures 4–9.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same PCA-based vector extraction, projection-based condition checking, thresholding, and conditional behavior-vector addition. Appendix A retains the same first-pass condition check and subsequent-token steering procedure.

E1.justification: Both use Sorry-Bench and Alpaca, the same five fine-grained condition categories, and the same four unseen categories: gambling, financial advice, privacy violence, and malware generation. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The base-model and unconditional activation-steering comparisons are retained. Table 2 keeps Llama 3.1 Instruct 8B and Llama 2 Chat 13B as reference models, and Figure 9c retains the same prompting baseline.

E3.justification: The reported sample counts, splits, models, refusal-classification procedure, and grid-search protocol match. Both retain 450 harmful and 500 harmless test prompts in Section 4, the 700/500 per-category training/test split in Section 5, and identical intervention settings in Table 4.

E4.justification: Both retain the same duality and threshold-modulation analysis, sample-size and runtime scaling, refusal-composition tests, and unseen-category and semantic-distance analyses. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains its 25th–75th percentile shading. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results match. For example, Table 3 retains CAST harmful/harmless refusal rates of 90.67%/2.20% for Qwen 1.5 1.8B and 83.33%/2.40% for Hermes 2 Pro. The qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The steering, projection, cosine-similarity, thresholding, and PCA formulations are unchanged, as is the reasoning about duality and modulation. No mathematical definition, derivation, or proof is substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims about selective refusal, logical composition, and control without weight optimization remain unchanged. The introduction modestly expands the released-resource contribution from a CAST library to a toolkit explicitly including demo datasets.

C2.justification: The substantive interpretations and limitations remain: saturation depends on existing representations, semantic distinctiveness affects domain restriction, suppression can conflict with induction, and imperfect refusal vectors and hyperparameter sensitivity limit performance. Shortening the conclusion does not remove these discussions.

D1.justification: v2 newly mentions released demo datasets but includes an unresolved GitHub-link placeholder in that contribution bullet; the actual repository link remains in the abstract. Figure 5 loses its NeuralDaredevil model identification. Appendix implementation details, model/data revisions, and hardware specifications otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to activation steering and other behavior-control approaches are unchanged. Differences in citation ordering and bibliography formatting do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes four contribution bullets into three labeled bullets, edits section headings, and condenses the conclusion. It removes the acknowledgements, internship footnote, and appendix contents list, while retaining most prose and the section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR typography and headers, restyles and reduces code listings, and adjusts figure placement and captions. Figure 12 moves from page 18 to page 17, and Figure 10 loses its explanation of the schematic black boundaries. The figures and tables themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The streamlined contributions and conclusion offer modest editorial benefits, but v2 introduces a visible link placeholder, removes Figure 5's model identification and Figure 10's schematic-boundary explanation, and makes appendix code smaller. These limited documentation and legibility losses slightly outweigh the streamlining. The scientific evidence, actual abstract repository link, and detailed technical appendices remain intact.
